0.en: What Form Morality Must Take in a Church
0.zh: 道德在教会中必定要采取的形式

en: The most important change has come about through the spread of Christianity, in the manner of promoting morality; out of this, after the church's transition from a private society into a state — out of a private affair it has become an affair of the state, and what by its nature is and was arbitrariness has become duty, and to some extent an external right of the church has grown out of it.

The church has laid down the principles of morality, and alongside this morality has at the same time given the means of making these principles one's own, and in particular has set up, under the name of casuistry, an extensive science about their application to individual cases.
zh: 最重要的变化，是通过基督教的传播、以促进道德的方式发生的；由此，随着教会从一个私人团体变成一个国——一件私事变成了一件国家的事——，按其本性是任意的、也一直是任意的那些东西变成了义务，而且其中一部分还长出了教会的外在法权。
教会立下了道德的原则，并且在道德之外还同时指出了把这些原则据为己有的手段，尤其还以决疑论的名义，就原则在个别场合的运用建立起一门内容繁多的学问。

en: In the church's moral system one main trait is that it is built upon religion and upon our dependence on the Godhead; the foundation on which it is built is not a fact of our spirit, a proposition that could be developed out of our consciousness, but something learned, and morality [is] therefore not a self-standing science, independent in its principles; the essence of morality is thus not grounded on freedom, not the autonomy of the will.
zh: 教会的道德体系有一个主要特征，就是它建立在宗教之上、建立在我们对神的依赖之上；它所依据的基础，并不是我们精神的一个事实、一条能从我们意识里发展出来的命题，而是学来的东西；所以道德并不是一门独立的、在原则上不依赖别的科学的学问；道德的本质因此不是建立在自由之上，不是意志的自律。

en: One begins with historical knowledge; this is prescribed which feelings and which state of mind it is to produce, gratitude and fear — in order to keep us faithful to our duties, whose criterion is God's good pleasure, which is known for some duties but must be artificially calculated from those for others.

This art of reckoning has been extended so far, and the number of duties thereby so endlessly multiplied, that little is left to free choice; and whatever is not, as duty in itself, exactly commanded or forbidden becomes fully important in ascetics, which no longer lets a single thought pass duty-free, no action, no involuntary glance, no enjoyment of whatever kind, joy, love, friendship, sociability go uncontrolled, but claims every stirring of the soul, every association of thoughts, every one of the thoughts that fly through a person's head from second to second, every feeling of well-being, and, by a reckoning similar to the way the system of the doctrine of happiness deduces duties, knows how to deduce a danger through a long series of inferences.

Ascetics further prescribes for the soul a host of exercises by which it is to be worked upon, and is an extensive science of tactics, which teaches one to manoeuvre artificially and regularly against every enemy of piety that each person has in his bosom, and that any situation, any view can become for him, and especially against the invisible hellish enemy.
zh: 人们是从历史知识开始的；这种知识被规定好了要产生哪些感受、哪种心境——感恩和畏惧——，好让我们忠于自己的义务；义务的标准在于神是否喜悦；有些义务的这一点是已知的，别的义务则必须人为地从已知的推算出来。

这门算术被扩展得如此之广，义务的数目也因此被无限地增多，以致留给自由任意的东西已经很少了；而那些本身作为义务并没有被直接命令或禁止的东西，在禁欲学里就更是要紧：它再也不放过任何一个念头，不放过任何行为、任何不由自主的一瞥、任何享受——不管是哪一种快乐、爱、友谊、交往——，全都要受它检查，而是把灵魂的每一次悸动、每一个念头的联结、每一秒从人脑子里飞过的每一个念头、每一种安适的感受都算进去；它用一套和幸福说体系推导义务差不多的算法，靠一长串推论，就能推导出一种危险来。
禁欲学还给灵魂规定了一大堆练习，要借这些练习对灵魂加以加工；它是一门内容繁多的战术学，教人如何用技巧、按规矩去对付虔诚的每一个敌人——这敌人每个人自己怀里都有，任何一种处境、任何一种看法都可能变成他的敌人——，尤其要对付那个看不见的地狱之敌。

en: To judge in every single case how one should act is, to be sure, very hard for the layman and the unlearned, for given the multitude of moral and prudential rules, several of them can come into collision in the very simplest matter, and it takes a well-practised acuteness to find one's way happily out of such now entangled cases, where of course sound common sense has not thought of all these precautions at all, and immediate feeling has usually grasped a more correct way of acting than the most learned casuists — and would not, as their decision commonly does, have omitted a good action because of a chance to sin that perhaps and remotely arises out of the action.

In all these rules of morality and prudence one has proceeded a priori, i.e. a dead letter has been laid at the foundation and a system erected on it, how man is to act, to feel, what movements this and that so-called truth is to produce — the legislative power over all, even the noblest powers of the soul, has been granted to memory.

Anyone into whom these threads of the system have not been woven from youth, and who has otherwise come to know human nature through experience of others and his own feeling, and now becomes acquainted with the system and is to live in it, finds himself in an enchanted world; in the man of the system he can recognize no being of his own kind; sooner than in him will he find nature in the fairy tales of the Orient and in our romances of chivalry, and he will not go so far astray there as on that path, if he wanted to base a system of physics on those fictions of the imagination and a psychology on these births of our day — and if he throws himself down before God and men as a poor sinner and a corrupted man, then, given the innate corruption of our nature, such a fault is not worth the trouble of acknowledging himself guilty of it before God, himself and others; even without that we are good for nothing, and a comfort in it is that we share this with all other people anyway, in comparison with whom each then believes he still has something in advance. — If then a man has run through the whole course of cognitions, feelings and states of mind prescribed by the church and has still got no further than another who lacked this whole apparatus, like so many virtuous people among the so-called blind heathen, and [if] he has indeed got very far in anxiousness and caution, submission and obedience, but has fallen behind or come away quite empty in courage, resolution, strength and other virtues, by which alone one becomes capable of furthering the best of individuals and of the state — what then has the human race gained by the church's laborious system of rules?

One would want to raise this question all the more if one considers the numerous multitudes of hypocrites in every such church, who possess all those cognitions, feelings, and the church's sayings too, and live and move in such church exercises; what strength can one ascribe to them, if they yet observed and did everything the church demands, and yet remain villains and are swindlers into the bargain?
zh: 要在每一个个别场合判断该怎样行动，对俗人和没学问的人来说确实非常难，因为道德规则和谨慎规则那么多，在最简单的事情上也可能有好几条互相冲突；要从这样一些如今纠缠不清的场合里幸运地脱身，得有一副训练有素的精明才行——当然，健全的常识根本没想过所有这些防备，而直接的感受通常抓到的行动方式，比最有学问的决疑论者还更正确；它也不会像决疑论者的裁决通常那样，因为从这行动里也许、而且很间接地会生出犯罪的机会，就干脆不做一件好事。
所有这些道德规则和明智规则，都是先天地做出来的，也就是说，拿一个死字母当了基础，在它上面搭起一个体系：人该怎样行动、怎样感受，这种那种所谓的真理该引起哪些活动——一句话，立法权被交给了记忆，让它管灵魂的一切力量，连最高贵的力量也归它管。

谁要是从小没有被织进体系里的这些线，而是靠对别人的经验和对自己的感受认识了人性，如今又接触了这个体系、还得生活在其中，那他就是待在一个着了魔的世界里；在体系人身上，他认不出任何一个和自己同类的存在者；比起在体系人身上，他倒更容易在东方童话和我们的骑士小说里找到自然，而且他在那里迷路的程度，也不会像在那条路上那么厉害——如果他竟想拿想象力的那些虚构来建立一个物理学的大厦，拿我们今天的这些产儿来建立一门心理学的话。又，如果他跪在神和人面前，把自己说成一个可怜的罪人、一个败坏的人，那么，鉴于我们天性中生来就有的败坏，这样的过错根本不值得费劲去在神、自己和别人面前认罪；就算不这样，我们本来也一无所用，而且这里还有个安慰：这一点我们反正和所有人一样，比起来每个人都还觉得自己略胜一筹。那么，如果一个人把教会规定的整套认识、感受和心境的行程都跑完了，却还是没有比另一个缺少这整套装置的人走得更远——就像所谓盲目的异教徒中许多有德之人那样——，如果他在胆怯和谨慎、顺从和服帖上走得很远，在勇气、果断、力量以及其他那些唯独能使人去促进个人和国家之至善的德性上却落在后面，甚至一无所获——那么，人类靠教会那套辛苦的规则体系究竟得到了什么呢？
只要想到每个这样的教会里都有大批伪善者——他们拥有所有那些认识、感受，也会念教会的箴言，就生活在并且活动于这类教会操练之中——，人们就更想提出这个问题了：他们既然遵守并做了一切教会要求的事，却仍旧是恶棍，而且还是骗子，那还能说他们有什么力量呢？

en: An advantage, and a great one, the state — or rather the holders of power in it, for the state itself is shattered in the process — has gained from this project of the church to work upon people's dispositions, namely a dominion, a despotism, which, after the suppression of all freedom of the will by the clergy, has a completely won game; civil and political freedom the church has taught people to despise as dung against the heavenly goods and the enjoyment of life, and just as the lack of means to satisfy physical needs robs the animal part of man of life, so the robbing of the enjoyment of the freedom of the spirit, of reason, brings death, a state in which people will feel the loss, the [want of] use of it, the longing for it as little as the dead body longs for food and drink. — Thus through Jesus' attempt to make his nation attentive to the spirit and the disposition, which in the observance of its laws must be alive if it is to become well-pleasing to God, through this attempt, under the church's regime, this complementum of the laws has again become rules and ordinances, which in turn always need such a complementum; and this attempt of the church has again failed; for the spirit, the disposition, is too ethereal a being to let itself be held fast in commanding letters and formulas or be presented in commanded feelings and states of mind.
zh: 国家——更确切地说，是国家里的当权者，因为国家本身在这个过程中被砸碎了——从教会这个想要影响人的意念的打算里得到了一个好处，而且是个大好处，那就是一种统治、一种专制：神职人员把意志的一切自由都压下去之后，这种专制就稳操胜券了。公民自由和政治自由，教会教人把它当作粪土去换天上的财富和生活的享受；正像缺少满足肉体需要的办法，会夺去人身上动物性的那部分生命一样，剥夺对精神自由、理性自由的享受，带来的也是死亡——在这种状态里，人们感觉不到这种丧失、[感觉不到]不去使用它，也感觉不到对它的渴望，就像死尸不会渴望饮食一样。耶稣曾试着让他的民族注意精神和意念——在遵守他们的律法时，这种精神和意念必须是活的，才能蒙神悦纳——可是在教会的治理下，正是这一尝试使律法的这个 complementum（补足物）又变成了规则和条例，而这些规则和条例又总是需要这样一种补足物；教会这一尝试也就再次失败了；因为精神、意念是太轻灵的一种东西，没法把它固定为发号施令的字句和公式，也没法把它表现成被命令的感受和心境。

en: Another evil that necessarily followed from this is that these feelings, which are to occur in the course of becoming better, and the actions that are regarded as expressions of such feelings — communion, confession, certain alms on the occasion of these and during divine service — are public, are brought before the ecclesiastical state or its officials, who, just because they are such officials, are supposed to be our friends.

In this public display of one's progress on the path of piety, no one will easily want to stay behind, so he joins in the feelings and their signs — and more the church cannot possibly command and bring about.
zh: 由此必然产生的另一个弊病是：这些在变好的过程中应当出现的感受，以及被看作这类感受之表现的行为——圣餐、告解、在这类场合和礼拜时施舍的某些赈济——都是公开的，都要呈交给教会这个国家或它的官员，而这些人正因为是这种官员，就应当是我们的朋友。
在这样公开展示自己在虔诚之路上取得的进步时，谁都不容易愿意落在后面，于是也跟着做那些感受和它们的标志——而更多的事，教会是根本命令不来、也办不到的。

en: Our customs too, insofar as they display feelings through outward signs, refer not so much to feelings one really has as to feelings one ought to have, as at the death of one's relatives one ought to feel more sadness than one always really feels, and the outward signs of this feeling are directed not so much by what one really feels as by what one ought to feel, and people have even agreed on the strength and the duration of the feeling; and since our public religion also refers to rules of feeling in these matters — as also in mourning and [the] fasting of Lent and the finery and good living of Easter days — and many of our customs do so, and these rules are supposed to hold universally, there is now so much empty, spiritless stuff in our usages, since the feeling has departed from them, while the same feeling is always still imposed on us in the rule.
Nothing has damaged monastic ascetics and casuistry so much as the greater cultivation of the moral sense among people and the better knowledge of the nature of the human soul47).
zh: 我们的风俗也一样：只要它们是用外在标志来表现感受，所指的就多半不是人现实中有的感受，而是人应当有的感受——比如亲人去世时，人应当感到的悲伤比现实中总是感到的更多，而这种感受的外在标志，所依据的也多半不是人现实中感觉到的东西，而是人应当感觉到的东西，甚至连感受的强度和持续时间，人们都商量好了；既然我们的公开宗教在这些方面——也像在斋期的哀悼和禁食、复活节的打扮和享乐上那样——以及我们的许多风俗，都涉及感受的规则，而这些规则又应当普遍有效，那么如今我们的习俗里就有那么多空洞的、没有精神的东西，因为感受已经从里面溜走了，可是规则却始终还是要求我们有那种感受。
对修士的禁欲学和决疑论损害最大的，莫过于人们道德感的更多培养，以及对人的灵魂本性的更好认识47)。

en: In this way the church has not only prescribed a multitude of outward actions by which we are partly to show honor to the Godhead directly and put ourselves in favor with it, and partly to produce such a mood and direction of our spirit as it demands of us, but the church has also directly prescribed the laws for our way of thinking, feeling and willing, and the Christians have again come to where the Jews were; what is characteristic of the Jewish religion — bondage under a law, from which the Christians so heartily wish themselves fortunate to have become free — is found again in the Christian church too.

The difference lies partly in the means, in that the religious duties of the Jews were in a certain sense also compulsory duties, as they partly are in the Christian church too, in that whoever neglects them is here and there still burned, but almost universally deprived of the rights of his state.

The most excellent means, which in fact also occurred among the Jews, is effect upon the imagination, only that the representations used by both are different — among the Christians they are pre-eminently
zh: 这样一来，教会不仅规定了许多外在行为——我们借这些行为，一部分是直接向神表示敬意、讨它的欢心，一部分是要借此产生它所要求的那种心境和精神方向——，而且教会还直接为我们的思想、感受和意欲的方式规定了法则，基督徒于是又回到了犹太人待过的地方；犹太教的特征——在律法之下的奴役，基督徒那么庆幸自己已经从中获得自由——在基督教会里又出现了。
差别有一部分在手段上：犹太人的宗教义务在某种意义上是强制性的义务，而在基督教会里它们也有一部分是强制性的，因为谁不尽这些义务，个别地方还会被烧死，但几乎普遍地会被剥夺他的国家权利。
最出色的手段——其实在犹太人那里也有——是对想象力起作用，只不过两者所使用的表象不同——在基督徒那里，主要是

zh: 高塔上架起惊怖的火，去攻取做梦人的想象，那里律法的火把昏暗地燃着。48)

en: The main difference is supposed to be that the Jews believed they did the Godhead enough with their outward ceremonies, whereas the Christians are impressed with the fact that everything depends solely on the disposition with which two people perform the same action; now the Christian's disposition is prescribed for him quite exactly, in the order of salvation not only the sequence of his necessary cognitions, which are indeed capable of being made clear, but also the sequence of the various states of mind that are to develop out of those and out of one another, is exactly traced out — and the church commands that this course be gone through — and that in the Christian church the contradictory addition of commanding feelings comes in as well, whereas in Judaism only actions were commanded; this difference is not of such a kind that the purpose of morality and religion, morality itself, would be brought about by it, but it is impossible in itself and was impossible for the church as well to bring forth on this path anything more than legality and craftsmanlike virtue and piety. — The necessary consequences of wanting to command feelings were and had to be these: self-deception, that one believed one had the prescribed feeling, believed one's feeling to agree with what one found described, whereas such an artificially produced feeling could impossibly equal the true, natural one either in strength or in worth; [the consequence] of this self-deception is either false calm, which sets a high value on these feelings produced in the spiritual hothouse and thinks much of itself, and is therefore weak where strength would now be needed, and, when such a person notices this himself, falls into helplessness, fear, mistrust of himself — a state of soul that is often driven to madness, just as he too often falls into despair who, with all good will and every possible effort, still believes he has not driven his feelings to the height that is required of him, and since he is in the field of feelings and can never arrive at any firm standard of his perfection (except perhaps through deceptions of the imagination), he will find himself in an anxiousness that lacks strength and resolution and finds some calm only in trust in the unlimited grace of the Godhead — only a small increase in the tension of the imagination turns this state likewise into madness and derangement.

The most usual effect is a kind of the self-deception cited above, where, with all the riches of spiritual feelings, one on the whole keeps one's character and the ordinary man dwells alongside the spiritual one, at most is fitted out by the latter with phrases and outward gestures, and in trade and dealings is the ordinary man, but on Sundays or among his brethren or before his prayer book is quite another; it is often too harsh to accuse such a character of actual hypocrisy; hypocrisy requires consciousness of the contradiction between the motives of the actions and the shield one hangs out in the process; in that former case this consciousness is very much missing, and the person has absolutely no unity; if these two kinds of disposition really come into collision, and the fleshly one has the upper hand, as is very commonly the case, then amid the enormous multitude of moral and ascetic commandments the latter cannot possibly lack one with which the offense can be brought into connection and can appear to the agent himself, under this cover, in a praiseworthy shape.

These subtleties have been driven furthest among the Catholics; the Lutheran church has above all thrown away most of the outward part, but has set up a system of feeling-statutes and rules, which is most consistently asserted and practised by the Pietists; for although these seem to be only a sect of this church, one cannot say that they have in anything deviated in their system of faith or morals from the statutes of their church; on the contrary, they seem only to express that same system more precisely, and if they appear to distinguish themselves from the great majority of Lutherans, it is because in the latter nature and sound common sense prevent the correspondence of their life and their feelings to their system.
On the whole, the Reformed seem most of all to make morality the main thing and to neglect ascetics.
zh: 主要差别据说在于：犹太人以为靠外在的仪式就为神做够了，而基督徒则被反复叮嘱，说这全看两个人做同一件事时所抱的意念；基督徒的意念如今给他规定得十分精确，在救恩次序里，不仅他那些必然的认识的次序——这些认识当然是可以讲清楚的——，就连各种心境从这些认识中、以及彼此之间应当发展出来的次序，都精确地画好了——教会还命令人把这套课程走完。而且在基督教会里，还多了一条自相矛盾的规定：命令人有感受，而在犹太教里毕竟只命令了行为。这一差别并不是那种能由此达成道德和宗教的目的、即达成道德的差别；按事情本身，教会也不可能靠这条途径产生出比合法性、比手艺式的德行和虔诚更多的东西。想要命令感受，其必然后果过去是、也必然是这些：自我欺骗，即人以为自己有了被规定的感受，以为自己的感觉和他在书上看到的描述是一致的，可是这样人为造出来的感受，绝不可能在力量上或在价值上比得上真实、自然的感受；这种自我欺骗的后果，要么是虚假的安心：它把在精神温室里培育出来的这些感受看得很高，自以为了不起，因此到了真正需要力量的地方反而软弱，而当这样一个人自己察觉到这一点时，就陷入无助、恐惧、对自己失去信任——这是一种常常被逼到发疯的灵魂状态；同样，另一个人也常常陷入绝望：他怀着全部善意、使出一切可能的努力，却仍旧认为自己没有把感受提高到要求于他的那个高度；既然他处在感受的领域里，又永远达不到一个衡量自己完善的固定尺度（除非靠想象力的欺骗），他就会处在一种胆怯不安之中，这种不安缺少力量和果断，只能在对神无限恩典的信任里找到一点安心——只要想象力的紧张稍微再增强一点，这种状态同样会变成疯狂和精神错乱。

最常见的后果是上面所说的自我欺骗的一种：人虽然有丰富的精神感受，整体上却仍旧保持原来的性格，那个寻常人和这个属灵的人住在一起，顶多被后者用些套话和外在的手势装点一下；在做买卖和日常往来中他是个寻常人，到了礼拜天、或者在弟兄们中间、或者在自己的祈祷书前，就完全是另一个人了。要指责这样一种性格是现实的伪善，往往太过严厉；伪善要求人意识到行为动机和自己挂出来的招牌之间的矛盾；而在前一种人那里，这种意识恰恰很缺，这个人根本没有任何统一性。这两种意念要是真的发生冲突，而肉体的那一种像通常那样占了上风，那么在道德和禁欲的无数戒律当中，它绝不可能找不到一条，可以把这过失和它联系起来，而且让行动者自己在这层遮盖之下，还显得样子可嘉。

这些烦琐的东西在天主教徒那里被推得最远；路德宗教会尤其把外在的东西大部分扔掉了，却立起了一套关于感受的戒律和规则的体系，而这套体系被虔敬派最一贯地主张和实行；因为虔敬派虽然看起来只是这个教会的一个教派，却不能因此说他们在自己的信仰体系或道德体系上偏离了教会的戒律；恰恰相反，他们似乎只是把那同一个体系表达得更精确；至于他们好像显得与大多数路德宗信徒不同，那是因为在后者那里，本性和健全的常识妨碍了他们的生活和感受同他们的体系相称。
总的说来，归正宗的人似乎最把道德当作主要的事情，而忽略禁欲学。

11.en: Necessity of the Origin of Sects

en: Given this project of the various Christian churches to fix, command and produce the disposition, the motives of the actions, partly through public statutes and ordinances, partly through the executive power necessary for it, and given the impossibility of ruling over human freedom by these means and of producing more than legality, there had to be, from time to time — or the church would have had to bring it about that in a part of the human race the character of humanity were irrevocably extirpated, that this deficiency were made an ineradicable character of a race — there had to be from time to time people who in this churchly legality, in a character such as ascetics is capable of forming, found the demands of their own heart unsatisfied and felt themselves capable of giving themselves a law of morality that would proceed from freedom49); if they did not keep their faith to themselves alone, they became founders of a sect, which, in case it was not suppressed by the church, spread, and the further it rolled on from its source, the more it again retained only the rules and laws of its founder, which for its followers were now no longer laws out of freedom but again church statutes; which in turn brought about the origin of new sects; and so on forever — first in the Jewish church, out of it the Christian sect arose, it became a church, in the bosom of this church new sects were again generated, which then also grew into churches, and so it must go on as long as the state misjudges the extent of its rights and either lets a state of a ruling church arise within itself or even associates itself with it and so again oversteps its powers. —50) The basic error that lies at the foundation of the whole system of a church is the misjudgment of the rights of each capacity of the human spirit, especially of the first among them, reason; and if reason has been misjudged by the church's system, then the church's system can be nothing other than a system of contempt for human beings.

The salutary separation of the domains of the powers of the human spirit, which Kant made for science — this separation has not been made by the legislation of the church, and centuries will still pass before the spirit of the Europeans, in active life, in legislation, will learn to recognize and to make that distinction, to which the correct feeling of the Greeks had brought them of itself.

For the moral commandments of reason are treated and set up in the Christian church, as in every church whose principle is pure morality, just like rules of the understanding51); the former are subjective, the latter objective; by the Christian church, on the other hand, the subjective element of reason is set up as a rule like something objective.
zh: 各个基督教会既然有这个用意：一部分靠公开的法规和戒律，一部分靠为此所需的执行权力，把意念、把行为的动机固定下来、命令出来、制造出来；而靠这些手段又不可能统治人的自由、不可能产生出比合法性更多的东西——那么，隔一段时间就必定会——否则教会就得做到在人类的一部分人身上不可挽回地根除人性的性格，把这一缺陷变成某个种族无法磨灭的性格——隔一段时间就必定会有些人，他们在这种教会合法性里、在禁欲学所能养成的那种性格里，觉得自己内心的要求没有得到满足，并且觉得自己有能力给自己立一条出于自由的道德法则49)。他们若不把自己的信仰只留给自己，就成了一个教派的创始人；这教派只要没被教会压下去，就会扩展开来，而且从源头往外滚得越远，就又只剩下了它创始人的规则和律法，而这些对它后来的追随者来说，也不再是出于自由的法则，而又是教会的法规了；于是又引出新教派的产生；就这样一直下去——先是在犹太教会里，从它里面产生了基督教的教派，它变成了教会，在这个教会的怀抱里又生出新的教派，这些教派随后也长成了教会；只要国家不认识自己权利的范围，要么让自己内部产生一个由占统治地位的教会构成的国家，要么干脆和它联合起来，从而又越出自己的权限，这种情形就得一直继续下去。50) 一个教会整个体系的根本错误在于：不承认人的精神每一种能力的权利，尤其是不承认其中第一种能力即理性的权利；而理性一旦被教会的体系不承认，教会的体系就只能是轻视人的体系。
人的精神各种力量各有其领域，康德为科学做出了这种有益的分割——教会的立法却没有做出这种分割；还要过好几个世纪，欧洲人的精神才会在行动的生活里、在立法中学会认识和做出那种区分——而希腊人凭他们正确的感觉，自己就已经达到了那种区分。
因为理性的道德诫命在基督教会里，也像在任何一个以纯粹道德为原则的教会里那样，被当作知性的规则来对待、来设立51)；前者是主观的，后者是客观的；而基督教会却把理性中主观的东西当作客观的东西，立为规则。

en: Reason sets up moral, necessary and universally valid laws; in this respect they are called objective by Kant, though in a different sense than the rules of the understanding; now to make these laws subjective, or into maxims, to find motives for them, this is the task where the attempts diverge infinitely.

That capacity of reason the theologians have seldom denied, and nowadays it is granted to it pretty generally — or if they have denied it, they understood by that chiefly the second thing, namely that reason is not able to give its law such motives as would be capable by themselves of procuring respect for the law and of making the will inclined to act in accordance with it; the Christian religion gives us objective motives, motives that are not the law itself.
zh: 理性建立起道德的、必然的、普遍有效的法则；就此而言康德把它们称为客观的，尽管含义不同于知性的规则；而把这些法则变成主观的、变成准则，为它们找到动力，这就是那个各种尝试无限分歧的任务。
理性的那种能力，神学家们很少否认，如今人们也差不多普遍承认它——或者，如果他们否认过，那么他们主要理解的是第二点，即理性没有能力给自己的法则配上这样的动力，这些动力本身能够为法则赢得敬重，并使意志倾向于照着法则行动；基督教宗教给我们的是客观的动力，是那些不是法则本身的动力。

en: The only moral motive, respect for the moral law, can be produced only in that subject in which this law is legislative, out of whose inner being it itself proceeds; but the Christian religion announces the moral law to us as something existing outside us, as something given, and must therefore strive to procure respect for it in another way.
Into the concept of a positive religion this mark could already be taken up, that it sets up the moral law before human beings as something given.

In this way virtue has become an art of a very entangled kind, whereas on the contrary an uncorrupted moral feeling, which may itself decide, is able to decide in the moment — an art that has manifold handgrips and exercises and that, like any other, is supposed to be learnable, but which has had the strange fate that, while all human arts have been perfected and one generation has learned from the other, the morality of human beings alone has not visibly increased, but, without being able to use the experience of the preceding generations, each must again learn from the beginning for himself.
Civil legislations and constitutions have the external rights of human beings as their object, the church constitution that which a human being owes to himself or to God.
What a human being owes to God and to himself, this the church claims to know, and at the same time it sets up a judgment seat before which it judges about it.

Before this seat it has drawn everything that can be divine in the actions and events of human beings, and has entered into its law book what human beings are to feel in the process, and in this way has set up an extensive moral code which contains in part what a human being is to do, in part what he is to know and believe, in part what he is to feel.

On the possession and handling of this code the whole legislative and judicial power of the church is founded; and if it is contrary to the right of reason of every human being that he be subjected to such a foreign code, then the whole power of the church is unlawful; and on the right to give himself his own law, to be accountable for its handling to himself alone, no human being can renounce, for with this alienation he would cease to be a human being.

But to hinder him in this is not the business of the state — that would mean wanting to compel the human being to be a human being, and would be violence. — The emergence of all sects in the Christian church in the middle and modern ages was founded on the feeling of individual human beings that they had the right to be their own lawgivers, but, born in barbarous times or in a class of the people condemned by its rulers to coarseness, the principle of such legislation was usually a heated, wild and disorderly imagination, among whose monstrosities a beautiful spark of reason sometimes flashed out, and in which nevertheless the inalienable human right was always asserted, to give oneself laws out of one's own bosom.52)
zh: 唯一道德的动力，即对道德法则的敬重，只能在这样一个主体里产生：这法则在这个主体里立法，是从他的内心里自己出来的；但基督教宗教却把道德法则宣布为我们之外存在的东西、被给予的东西，因此它必须设法以另一种方式为这法则赢得敬重。
实证宗教的概念里早就可以收进这样一个标志：它把道德法则当作被给予的东西摆到人面前。
这样一来，美德就变成了一门非常纠缠的艺术，而反过来，一种未经败坏的道德感受，它自己有权作决定，是能在当下就作出决定的——这门艺术有五花八门的手法和练习，也该像别的艺术一样能够学会，但它在这里却有一种古怪的命运：一切人类的艺术都完善起来了，一代人向另一代人学，唯独人的道德没有明显地增长，反而每个人都不能利用前几代人的经验，只能自己从头再学一遍。
市民的立法和宪法以外在的人的权利为对象，教会的宪制则以人对自己或对上帝所欠的东西为对象。
人欠上帝什么、欠自己什么，教会声称自己知道，并且同时设立一个审判席，在它面前对此作出裁断。
它把人的行为和事件中一切可能是神圣的东西都拉到这审判席前，并且把人在这里应当感受什么也记进了它的法典，就这样立起一部内容冗长的道德法典，其中一部分规定人该做什么，一部分规定他该知道什么、相信什么，一部分规定他该感受什么。
教会的全部立法权和司法权都建立在对这部法典的占有和运用上；如果一个人受这样一部异己的法典支配违背了每个人理性的权利，那么教会的全部权力就是不合法的；而自己给自己立法、只对自己负责运用这部法典，这权利没有人能放弃，因为一旦让渡了它，他就不再是人了。

但阻止他这样做，不是国家的事——那等于想要强迫人成为人，那就是暴力。—— 基督教教会中一切教派在中世纪和近代的出现，都建立在个别的人的那种感受上：他们有权自己做自己的立法者；但既然生在野蛮的时代，或者生在一个被自己的统治者注定要粗野的民众阶层里，这种立法的原则通常就是一种发热的、狂野的、无序的想象力，在它的怪胎中间有时会闪出一点理性的美丽火花，而其中终究总是坚持着那不可让渡的人的权利：从自己的胸中给自己立法。52)

en: 53) A positive faith is such a system of religious propositions as is supposed to have truth for us for the reason that it is commanded to us by an authority to which we cannot refuse to submit our faith.

In this concept there occurs first of all a system of religious propositions or truths which, independently of our holding them true, are to be regarded as truths, which, even if they had never been known to any human being and never held true by any human being, would yet remain truths, and which in this respect are often called objective truths — now these truths are also to become truths for us, subjective truths.

Those truths that concern the understanding or the reason are to be received by these as such, those that contain commands for our will are to be received by it as maxims, and indeed their first command, the condition of all the rest, is the one that commands us to hold those truths as such — for this is commanded to us by an authority which we absolutely cannot refuse to obey.

This concept belongs essentially to the concept of a positive faith, that it is a duty for us to believe; for historical faith, and further the faith in what parents, educators, friends tell us, is likewise a faith on authority, only this faith has its ground in a trust in these persons that is arbitrary, that rests for the most part on the credibility that their reports given to us have for us, whereas faith in the authority of the positive doctrines is nothing that lies in our arbitrariness, and the trust in it must be grounded before all acquaintance with or judgment of the content of the given doctrines.

God's right over us and the duty of our obedience to him rests on this, that he is our mighty lord and master and we are his creatures and subjects — on his benefits toward us and our duty of gratitude, further on this, that he is the source of truth and we are ignorant, blind: about these titles of right we remark only that the two latter already presuppose a certain love of truth, already a kind of moral disposition, that especially the one taken from God's benefits proceeds from what is first to be proved — namely our obligation to positive religion is in this case derived from this, that it is a benefit and to obey out of gratitude really means as much as doing it to please God, giving him joy, etc. The first ground of our obligation is the properly weighty one, especially since one thereby turns to the sensuous human being, in whom a moral disposition is first to be produced: that from this relation to God there belongs to this being a kind of right of coercion, whose exercise he can never escape — from a lord on earth the slave can hope to withdraw, to pull himself out of the circle of his power; but not so from God: if he took the wings of the dawn, you are there; if he crept away into the lowest sea, you are there too.

Whoever acknowledges this superior power of a being not only over the drives of his life — for such a power everyone must acknowledge, whether under the name of nature, Fatum or providence — but also such a superior power over his spirit, over the whole extent of his being, cannot withdraw from a positive faith.
The capacity for such a faith necessarily presupposes loss of the freedom of reason, of its self-sufficiency, which can set nothing against a foreign power.

Here is the first point from which all belief or unbelief in a positive religion proceeds, and at the same time the center around which all disputes about it turn, and even if it does not come to clear consciousness, it nevertheless constitutes the ground of all submissiveness or obstinacy.

Here the orthodox must hold fast, here concede nothing; — even if they admit that morality is truly the absolute and highest end of humanity, even if they admit that reason is capable — since they cannot deny what happens before their eyes — of building a pure system of morality, they must nevertheless assert that it is nevertheless by itself incapable of procuring for itself the primacy over the inclinations, of realizing its demands, and they must necessarily determine these demands, the final end of humanity, in such a way that, if not in the positing of it, yet in its executability, the human being is dependent on a being outside him.

Once this incapacity of reason and the dependence of our whole being are presupposed, which is the necessary condition of everything that follows, the proof that a certain religion, e.g. the Christian religion, is such a positive religion given by God is to be conducted entirely historically, and this is now all the easier because, with the acknowledgment of our servitude, we have thereby laid the standard of another examination out of our hands, have entirely given up the right to ask after inner grounds, after its rationality, to examine the appropriateness of the narrated events to the laws of experience. — The question after rationality or irrationality is here a wholly idle question, which can perhaps be raised out of boredom, but which absolutely must not be regarded as contributing to the decision of my faith — before the higher court, once it is acknowledged, all lower ones must be silent.

What is therefore held true because it is rational never lies within the scope of my positive faith, although it can happen that what I at first believed merely because belief in it was commanded to me, I afterwards believe because I now find it appropriate to my reason, because I have convinced myself of it from grounds; that the whole content of a positive religion is capable of finally being held true out of one's own reason, this only another can expect or demand, who is free of this positive faith, or by a believer the reduction of his positive doctrines to reason can be undertaken only, say, in order to satisfy such an outsider.

Rather, if inquiry were held about it, the opposite would be to be expected from a religion revealed by God, which therefore contains divine truths, i.e. truths thought by God, that the thoughts of God cannot be grasped, cannot be measured by human reason. — How then is a positive faith in such truths conceivably possible, how can they become subjective; how is the human mind affected in this state, how active, how passive?
The expressions that a faith is a lively conviction, driving to action, accompanied by feelings, are too indeterminate for much to be said to us by them.
zh: 53) 实证信仰是这样一种宗教命题的体系：它对我们之所以应当具有真理性，是因为它是由一个权威命令给我们的，而我们无法拒绝把自己的信仰交给这个权威。
在这个概念里，首先出现的是一个宗教命题或真理的体系，这些命题或真理不依赖于我们是否信之为真，就应当被看作真理，即使它们从来不曾为任何人所知、从来不曾被任何人信之为真，它们仍然是真理，就此而言人们常把它们叫作客观真理——现在这些真理也应当成为对我们而言的真理，成为主观真理。
那些涉及知性或理性的真理，应当由知性和理性作为真理接受下来，那些包含对我们意志的诫命的真理，应当由意志作为准则接受下来，而其中第一条诫命、其余一切的条件，就是命令我们把那些真理当作真理来持守的那一条——因为这是由一个权威命令我们的，我们对它绝对无法拒绝服从。
这个概念本质上属于实证信仰的概念：相信对我们来说是一种义务；因为历史性的信仰，以及相信父母、教育者、朋友对我们说的话，同样是一种基于权威的信仰，只不过这种信仰的根据在于对这些人的信赖，而这种信赖是任意的，多半建立在那些人对我们所作的报道本身对我们具有的可信性上；与此相反，相信实证学说的权威，却不是我们任意范围内的事，对它的信赖必须在认识或评判所给学说的内容之前就已经建立。

上帝对我们的权利和我们服从他的义务，根据在于他是我们强大的主人和主宰，而我们是他的造物和臣民——在于他对我们的恩惠和我们感恩的义务，还在于他是真理的源泉，而我们是无知的人、盲人：关于这些权利的名义，我们只指出一点，后两种已经预设了对真理的某种爱、某种道德意向，尤其是从上帝的恩惠取来的那一种，是从还有待证明的东西出发的——就是说，在这种情况下我们对实证宗教的义务是从它是恩惠推论出来的，而出于感恩去服从，其实就等于讨上帝欢喜、让他高兴等等。我们义务的第一个根据才是真正有分量的那个根据，尤其因为人们借此针对的是感性的人，而道德意向在他身上还有待产生：从与上帝的这种关系中，这个存在者获得一种强制权利，它的行使他永远逃不掉——对一个地上的主人，奴隶还可以指望躲开，从他的权力范围里抽身出去；但对上帝却不能这样：他若展开清晨的翅膀，你也在那里；他若躲进最深的海里，你也在那里。
谁承认一个存在者不仅对他的生命冲动有这种优势——因为这样的优势每个人都必须承认，不论它叫自然、命运还是护佑——而且对他的精神、对他存在的全部范围也有这种优势，谁就无法从实证信仰中脱身。
对这样一种信仰的能力，必然以丧失理性的自由、丧失理性的自主为前提，因为这样的理性对一种异己的权力拿不出任何东西来抵抗。
这里是第一个点，一切对实证宗教的信或不信都从它出发，同时它也是中心，有关此事的一切争执都围着它转；即使它没有达到清晰的意识，它也构成了全部顺从或抗拒的根据。
在这里正统派必须守住，在这里什么也不能让；——即使他们承认道德在现实中是人类绝对而最高的目的，即使他们承认理性有能力——因为他们无法否认眼前发生的事——建立一套纯粹道德的体系，他们也必须坚持说，理性单凭自己毕竟没有能力取得对偏好的优先地位，没有能力实现它的要求，并且他们必须必然地把这些要求、把人类的终极目的规定成这样：即使不是在确立它的时候，至少在实行它的时候，人依赖于他之外的一个存在者。

一旦预设了理性的这种无能和我们整个存在的依赖，而这是一切后续东西的必然条件，那么要证明某个宗教、比如基督教宗教，是这样一种由上帝给予的实证宗教，就完全要用历史的方式来作，而这就更容易了，因为随着我们承认自己的奴役状态，我们也就因此对另一种检验的尺度撒了手，完全放弃了追问内在根据、追问它是否合乎理性的权利，也完全放弃了考察所讲述的事件是否合乎经验法则的权利。—— 合不合乎理性的问题在这里是一个完全多余的问题，或许可以出于无聊提一提，但绝对不可以被看作对决定我的信仰有所贡献——在一个已经被承认的更高法庭面前，所有较低的法庭都必须沉默。
因此，因为合乎理性而被信以为真的东西，从来就不在我的实证信仰范围之内，尽管可能发生这样的事：我起初仅仅因为有人命令我相信它才相信的东西，后来我相信它，是因为我现在觉得它合乎我的理性，是因为我凭根据被它说服了；一个实证宗教的全部内容是否终究能够凭自己的理性被信以为真，这只有另一个不受这种实证信仰束缚的人才能期待或要求，或者，一个信徒把实证学说归结到理性，也许只能是为了让这样一个外人满意才去做的。
如果对此真要追问，那么从一个由上帝启示的宗教——它因而包含着神圣的真理，即上帝所想的真理——那里，反倒应当期待相反的东西：上帝的思想是人的理性不能把握、不能衡量的。——那么，对这些真理的实证信仰如何可能设想，它们如何能成为主观的；人的心在这种状态中如何被触动，如何活动，如何承受？
说一种信仰是一种活泼的、促使人行动的、伴有感受的确信，这些说法太不确定，靠它们对我们说不出多少东西。

en: The Christian religion contains in part commands about cognitions of objects, with their practical moments, in part commands about actions.
zh: 基督教宗教一部分包含关于对象之认识的诫命，连同这些认识的实践环节，一部分包含关于行动的诫命。

en: The possibility of communicating to another one's experiences and thoughts presupposes that he has already had similar ones, which we now show him in another connection and set him the task of combining in the way we now indicate to him; presupposes the capacity to produce in himself those activities that we designate to him; now the truths of the Christian religion that relate to the cognitive faculty relate in part to the imagination, in part to the understanding, in part to the reason.
zh: 把自己经验和思想传达给别人的可能性，前提是他已经有过类似的体验和思想，我们现在把它们放在另一种联系里指给他看，并且给他任务，要他按我们现在指出的方式把它们联结起来；这可能性还以在他自身中产生我们向他指明的那些活动的能力为前提；而基督教宗教中涉及认识能力的那些真理，则一部分涉及想象力，一部分涉及知性，一部分涉及理性。

en: Historical truths that agree with our other laws of experience the imagination takes up, with the understanding's consent, whereby nothing in them is new to it except the connection into which it is now directed to bring representations it already had before; it takes them up at the same time with the accompanying representation that these were actual experiences, that feelings were present which had occasioned the understanding to an activity necessary for all human beings to whom these feelings would have been given; this is what faith signifies here. - But now there occur historical truths of which a somewhat practised understanding at once sees that they contradict its laws, and which it is therefore inclined to reject, like all miracles and other supernatural events; it is not satisfied by one's referring to supersensible causes, for such an answer it does not understand at all, nothing at all is thereby said to it - how then can the duty to believe be satisfied?

The imagination is completely satisfied with that indication of a supernatural cause - to it this is a matter of complete indifference -, but the understanding rejects its poem and allows it no objection at all in the question about the reality or non-reality of a representation; so a higher capacity, before which the understanding itself must fall silent, has to be brought into play, and faith is made a matter of duty and relegated to a domain of the supersensible, in which the understanding may no longer appear at all; in this respect to believe means as much as to hold fast, out of duty, that is, here out of fear of the mighty ruler, to a connection of events that is given to the imagination and in which the understanding always seeks another one, to compel the understanding thereby to lend its own hands to this business, which is an abomination to it, and to lend the concept of cause, but, as soon as it wants to meddle further there, at once to remove its demands from consciousness, to bring the connection given to the imagination to consciousness and by holding fast to it to give that other no room.
zh: 历史真理，凡是同我们其余的经验法则相合，想象力便在知性的准许下把它接受下来，其中对想象力说来，除了它如今奉命把先前已有的那些表象带进去的那个联系以外，再没有什么新东西；它同时连带接受这样一个附带的表象：这些是现实的经历，当时是存在着感受的，这些感受曾促使知性去从事一种活动，而这对一切被给予了这些感受的人说来都是必然的；在这里，信仰所意味的就是这个。——可是如今出现了一些历史真理，一个稍经训练的知性立刻看出它们同它的法则相矛盾，于是它倾向于把它们抛弃，就像对待一切奇迹和其他超自然的事件一样；人们对超感性原因的推诿并不能使它满意，因为这样一种回答它根本不懂，对它说来这等于什么也没说——那么，如今怎么才能履行相信的义务呢？

想象力对那指出一个超自然原因的说法完全满意——这对它完全无所谓——，可是知性却抛弃了它的诗作，而且在关于一个表象是实在还是非实在的问题上根本不许它插嘴；所以必须把一个更高的能力拉进来，连知性自己在它面前也得沉默，而信仰则被弄成一件义务的事，并被推到一个超感性的领域里，知性在那里再也不许露面；在这个意义上，相信就等于：把一个被给予想象力的、而知性在其中总要寻找另一个联系的事件联系，出于义务、也就是说在这里出于对那位强大主宰者的畏惧，牢牢抓住不放，并且在这件事上强迫知性自己动手去干这件对它说来是可憎的事，去出借原因这个概念，可是一旦知性想在那里多插一手，就立刻把它的要求从意识里清除出去，把被给予想象力的那个联系带到意识里来，并且通过抓住这个联系而不给那个要求留任何余地。

en: The practical moments, then, are given to reason in order to satisfy its demands; they do not bear upon the will so as to determine it to actions, but upon reason, which makes demands on the will and on the sensible world, or [upon] the law.

In the system of a positive religion reason is allowed only demands upon the sensible world which this religion promises to satisfy; demands upon the will are made by the law of the ruler, by positive religion itself, which promises support in this -: namely, this will, which has had no faith in its strength and, with the [strength] it still trusts itself to have, feels itself incapable of reaching the correspondence to the ideal that positive religion sets before it, receives the assurance of receiving help from above and support. - In this faith there is raised to consciousness and reflected upon that which lay at the ground of the possibility of a positive faith in general, the moral powerlessness and the feeling of being a machine that indeed still represents and is driven by given representations - there is reflected upon our unfamiliarity with the strength of this machinery, upon the inability, often tested by us, to be driven by certain representations, and with this is connected the hope that the first mover of this work, as a good and compassionate lord, will take it up and help it along where it is about to come to a standstill.

The human being caught up in positive faith here makes his whole condition, faithfully, into the object of his reflection, only that, just as he is otherwise determined by the representations given him in positive religion, here he does not think this determination as having passed through the medium of representation, but [thinks] that it will bear upon his activity, his essence itself.

As regards the demands of practical reason that positive religion promises to satisfy, they are of two kinds; some of them it [sc. reason] wishes to see realized, but before the realization of others it would be afraid - for both the positive religion promises to set it at rest.

Already the expression "reason wishes" or "it is afraid" indicates that sensibility comes into play here, that it would perhaps really be this which [suggests] to reason to make those demands, and that it is really this which wants to be satisfied. - How does reason come, in the postulate, especially famous in more recent times and occurring among all peoples, of the harmony of happiness with morality, to a demand upon something that in this respect it recognizes as independent of itself, as indeterminable?

Reason, which in some subject or other has grown to a degree of dominion, of power, gives to consciousness this feeling of ought, of ruling; if it thereupon turns to the will, which has a determinate object of drive, then this will is active according to the form given by reason, summons up the physical forces; if these conquer or succumb in the struggle with foreign, resisting forces and the will has [thereby] remained steadfast, then reason has been satisfied in every case, and if someone has died the death of honour or for fatherland or virtue, then only in our times has one been able to say that the man would have been worthy of a better fate.

Where reason finds a will that is more dominated by sensible inclinations, and where it seldom finds an occasion to turn to it, in such subjects sensibility hears its voice, its ought; and it explains this according to its own needs and interprets this ought of reason as a longing for happiness, which longing is, however, distinguished in this from the sensible demand of happiness, that it rests upon a voice of reason, that it presupposes a power of this to be able to pronounce an ought - and this demand, as it were legitimated by reason, is then called worthiness of happiness, and unworthiness of the same is called an incapacity of reason to pronounce an ought, a succumbing of the same and thus also a powerlessness against external circumstances.

In both cases reason does not demand happiness immediately - this concept belongs to it as little as sensation belongs to the understanding -, it gives to consciousness only its ought (or not), which is apprehended by sensibility; that [reason] determines nothing at all as to what the object of this ought shall be, it has no object of its dominion.

Even thus amalgamated with sensibility, reason demands the realization of its object55), and since it cannot realize this mixture, in that it is weakened and sullied by the admixture of nature, it demands a foreign being to which belongs the dominion over nature, which it now misses and which it can now no longer disdain.
zh: 实践的诸环节呢，是被给予理性用来满足它的种种要求的；它们并不针对意志，以便把意志规定去行动，而是针对那向意志和感性世界提出要求的理性，或者说针对法则。

在一个实证宗教的体系里，理性只被允许对感性世界提出种种要求，而这个宗教许诺去满足这些要求；对意志提出要求的是主宰者的法律，是实证宗教本身，它在此处许诺给予支持——也就是说，这个意志对自己的力量从不曾有过信心，又凭它自认还拥有的那份力量，感到自己不可能达到同实证宗教给它摆出的那个理想的相称，它于是得到保证，说会从上面得到帮助和支持。——在这种信仰里，那曾为一种实证信仰之可能性的根基的东西被提升到意识并受到反思，即道德上的软弱无力，以及那种觉得自己虽还在表象、却是被给予的表象所驱动的一台机器的感受——人们反思我们对自己这套齿轮装置的强弱并不了解，反思我们常常亲身体验到的、无法被某些表象驱动的无能，并且与此结合在一起的是这样一种希望：这套装置的第一推动者，会像一个善良而慈悲的主宰那样，在它要卡住的地方把它接过去、帮它一把。
处在实证信仰中的人在这里把自己的整个状态忠实地弄成自己反思的对象，只不过，正如他平时是被实证宗教里给予他的那些表象所规定，他在这里并不设想这种规定是经过表象这一媒介的，而是设想它将直接落到他的活动、他的本质本身上。
至于实证宗教许诺去满足的那些实践理性的要求，它们有两类；有一些它（即理性）是愿意看到实现的，而在另一些实现之前它却会害怕——对这两者，实证宗教都许诺使它安心。
单是"理性愿意"或者"它害怕"这样的说法就已经表明，感性在这里也掺和进来了，也许真正是它给理性出主意去提出那些要求的，而真正想要得到满足的其实就是它。——在近来特别出名、又在一切民族那里都出现的那个要求幸福与伦理相和谐的公设里，理性怎么会对某种它在这方面承认为独立于自己、无法规定的东西提出要求呢？

理性只要在某个主体里长到一定程度的统治、一定的权力，就把这种应当、这种统治的感受给予意识；如果它借此转向那个具有某个确定欲求对象的意志，那么这个意志就按理性所给的形式活动起来，调动起物理的力量；这些力量在同外来的、抗拒的力量作斗争时获胜或者败下阵来，而意志（在这当中）始终没有动摇，那么理性在任何情况下都得到了满足；至于有人为荣誉、为祖国或者为美德而死，那只有在我们这个时代才有人说得出：这人本该配得上更好的命运。

哪里理性遇到一个更多受感性偏好支配的意志，哪里它很少有机会转向这个意志，在这样一些主体里，感性就听到理性的声音、它的应当；感性按自己的需要来解释这一点，并且把理性这个应当解释为一种对幸福的渴求，而这种渴求又与感性的幸福要求有这点不同：它建立在一个理性的声音之上，它预设了理性有说出一个应当的权力——这个仿佛由理性使之合法的要求，这时就叫作配享幸福，而配不上幸福则叫作理性没有能力说出一个应当，叫作理性败下阵来，因而也叫作面对外部情况的无力。
在两种情况下，理性都不是直接要求幸福——这个概念对它说来就像感受对知性说来一样谈不上——，它只是把它的应当（或者不应当）给予意识，而这由感性去领会；那个应当的对象该是什么，理性根本没有规定，它没有自己统治的对象。
即便这样同感性混在一起，理性还是要求实现它的对象55），而由于它无法实现这个混合物——因为掺进了自然，它已被削弱、被弄脏——，它便要求一个异己的本质，这个本质具有对自然的统治，而那统治正是它现在所缺少、现在再也不能鄙弃的。

en: In this respect faith means the lack of consciousness that reason is absolute, is completed in itself, - that its infinite idea must be created only by itself, purely, without foreign admixture, - that this can be completed only by removing precisely this intruding foreign element, not by an assimilation of it.

The final end of reason, conditioned in this way, yields the moral faith in the existence of God, which cannot be practical insofar as it [could not] impel the will to realize that final end, but only perhaps the part of the final end that depends on it, to which it is made all the more willing by the consideration that sensibility will find its account in it too.

Whoever - as for example a republican or a warrior who fights not exactly for a fatherland, but still for honour - has thus set himself an end of his existence in which the second piece, happiness, is not to be found, he has an end whose realization depends entirely on him and therefore needs no foreign assistance.

Positive religion supports that moral faith further through images, through data for the imagination, to which it brings that object closer by making it so much an object that it relates that it was given to human beings here and there in experience.
Another famous need of reason, to which it can give itself absolutely no satisfying answer, is the demanded reassurance concerning the necessary punishments that must follow upon immorality.
zh: 在这个意义上，信仰就意味着缺乏这样一种意识：理性是绝对的，是在自身中完成了的，——它的无限观念必须只由它自己、纯粹地、不带异己的掺和创造出来，——而这个观念只有靠把那自行挤进来的异己东西排除掉才能完成，不能靠把它同化过来完成。
理性以这种方式被规定了的终极目的，给出对上帝存在的道德信仰，这种信仰不能是实践的，因为它并不能推动意志去实现那个终极目的，而也许只能推动那个终极目的中依赖于意志的那一部分；而由于考虑到感性在这里也会得到自己的好处，意志就更加愿意去做这一部分。
谁要是——例如一个共和派，或者一个并非正好为祖国、但毕竟为荣誉而战的战士——这样为自己定下了一个生存的目的，而其中找不到第二块即幸福，他所拥有的这个目的的实现在于他，因而无需任何外来的帮助。
实证宗教还用图像、用给想象力的材料来支持那种道德信仰，它借此把那个对象拉近，办法是把它弄得如此是一个对象，以至于它讲述说，这个对象在这里那里曾在经验中被给予人们。
理性的另一个著名的需要，是它对此根本给不出任何令人满意的回答的，就是人们所要求的、关于不道德必然要招来的那些惩罚的安心。

en: 56) Every people had its own objects of the fantasy, its gods, angels, devils or saints, who live on in the traditions of the people, whose story and deeds the nurse tells the children and [thereby] draws them to herself through the impression on their imagination and makes those stories lasting. - Besides these creatures of the imagination, there live in the memory of most peoples, especially of free peoples, the old heroes of the history of their fatherland, - the founders or liberators of the states almost fewer still than the brave ones from the times when the people united into a state standing under civil laws.

These heroes do not live isolated, alone in the fantasy of peoples; their story, the remembrance of their deeds, is tied to public festivals, national games, to many an inner arrangement or external relation of the state, to well-known houses and regions, to public temples and other monuments.

Every people that received its own religion and constitution, or else a part of the same and of its culture, from foreign nations, but had fully appropriated the same to itself, - Egyptians, Jews, Greeks, Romans have had such a national fantasy.

The old Germans too, Gauls, Scandinavians had their Walhalla, where their gods dwelt, their heroes, who lived in their songs, whose deeds inspired them in battles or at the meals filled their soul with great resolutions; they had their sacred groves, where these divinities were nearer to them.
zh: 56) 每个民族都有它自己的想象力的对象，它的神、天使、魔鬼或者圣徒，这些在民族的传统里继续活着，他们的故事和事迹由奶妈讲给孩子听，并通过给孩子想象力留下的印象把孩子们拉到自己身边，使那些故事固定下来。——除了这些想象力的造物，在大多数民族、尤其是自由民族的记忆里，还活着他们祖国历史上的古老英雄，——国家的创立者或解放者，几乎比那些生活在民族尚未结合为一个受市民法律支配的国家之前的勇敢者还少。
这些英雄并不是孤立地、单独地活在民族的想象力里；他们的故事、对他们事迹的回忆，系于公共的节日、民族竞技，系于国家许多内在的制度或者对外的关系，系于人人熟知的房屋和地区，系于公共的神庙和其他纪念物。
每个民族，凡是它自己的宗教和宪法，或者其中一部分以及它的文化是从外族那里得来的，但它已把这一切完全据为己有，——埃及人、犹太人、希腊人、罗马人都有过这样一种民族想象力。
古代日耳曼人、高卢人、斯堪的纳维亚人也各有自己的瓦尔哈拉，他们的神住在那里，他们的英雄活在自己的歌里，他们在战斗中受这些英雄事迹的激励，或者在宴饮时用伟大的决心充实自己的灵魂；他们也有自己的圣林，那些神祇在那里离他们更近。

en: Christianity has depopulated Walhalla, cut down the sacred groves and extirpated the fantasy of the people as shameful superstition, as a devilish poison, and has given us instead the fantasy of a people whose climate, whose legislation, whose culture, whose interest is foreign to us, whose history stands in absolutely no connection with us.

In the imagination of our people there lives a David, a Solomon, but the heroes of our fatherland slumber in the history books of the scholars, and for these an Alexander, a Caesar etc. have just as much interest as the history of a Charlemagne or Frederick Barbarossa.

Apart perhaps from Luther among the Protestants, who else could our heroes be, we who were never a nation? which would be our Theseus, who founded a state and gave it laws; where are our Harmodiuses and Aristogeitons, to whom as liberators of our land we would sing scolia?

The wars that have devoured millions of Germans were wars of the ambition or of the independence of the princes, the nation only a tool, which, even if it fought with bitterness and rage, in the end still did not know how to say: why? or what have we gained?

The Reformation and the bloody assertion of the right to make such a one is one of the few events in which a part of the nation has taken an interest, and indeed an interest that did not evaporate with the cooling of the imagination, as did that in the Crusades, but in which the feeling of a lasting right was active, the right to follow one's own conviction, won or preserved in one's religious opinions; but apart from the annual readings of the Augsburg Confession customary in some Protestant churches, which usually bores every listener, and apart from the cold sermon that follows it: which is the festival that celebrated the remembrance of that event?

It seems as though the holders of power in church and state would gladly see to it that the remembrance that our forefathers once felt this right and that thousands could risk their lives on the assertion of such a right, that the remembrance of this slumber in us, indeed that it not be kept alive.
zh: 基督教把瓦尔哈拉弄得空无一人，把圣林砍倒，把民族的想象力当作可耻的迷信、当作魔鬼的毒药连根铲除，而给我们的补偿是一个民族的想象力，这个民族的气候、立法、文化、利益对我们都是陌生的，它的历史同我们完全没有一点联系。
在我们民族的想象力里活着一个大卫、一个所罗门，可是我们祖国的英雄却在学者的历史书里沉睡，而对这些学者说来，一个亚历山大、一个凯撒等等，同一个查理大帝或者红胡子腓特烈的历史一样有意思。
除了新教徒那里的路德也许算一个，我们还能有谁是自己的英雄呢，我们从来就不曾是一个民族？谁能是我们的忒修斯，创立一个国家并给它立下法律；我们的哈尔莫狄俄斯和阿里斯托革同在哪里，我们能作为祖国的解放者向他们唱饮酒歌？
那些吞掉了千百万德意志人的战争，是诸侯的虚荣心或者诸侯独立的战争，民族只是工具；就算它打得满腔怨愤、怒火中烧，到头来它还是说不清：为什么？或者我们得到了什么？

宗教改革以及为有权进行这样一场改革而流的血，是少数几件让民族的一部分人发生过兴趣的事情之一，而且这种兴趣并不像对十字军的那份兴趣那样随着想象力的冷却而蒸发掉，其中起作用的是对一种持久权利的感受，即有权在自己的宗教见解中遵从自己赢得或保持下来的确信；可是，除了在某些新教教会里习以为常的一年一度朗读《奥格斯堡信纲》——这通常让每个听众都觉得无聊——以及随后那篇冷冰冰的布道之外：哪一个节日纪念过那件事呢？
看来教会和国家的掌权者倒乐意看到：我们的祖先曾经感受到这项权利、曾有成千上万的人敢于为坚持这样一项权利而拼上性命，对这件事的纪念在我们心里沉睡，是的，别让它活着保持下去。

en: Whoever lived for a year within the walls of the city of Athens without knowing its history, its culture and its legislation, could get to know it fairly well from its festivals.
zh: 谁要是不了解雅典城的历史、它的教养和立法，却在它的城墙里住上一年，也能从那些节庆对它了解得相当清楚。

en: So without religious imagination that would have grown on our soil and would be connected with our history, absolutely without any political imagination, there creeps about among the common people only here and there a remnant of an imagination of its own under the name of superstition, which as belief in ghosts keeps alive the memory of a hill on which knights once carried on their mischief, or of a house where monks and nuns haunted or where a steward or a neighbour held to be unfaithful has still found no rest in the grave, or which, as the offspring of an imagination that does not draw from history, fools weak or evil people with the possibility of a witch's power — wretched and sad remnants of an attempted independence and of an attempted property, which to root out completely is presented as a duty of the whole enlightened class of the nation and is the general tone — through which disposition of the finer part of the nation, apart from the unformability and roughness of the material itself, the possibility of ennobling that remnant of mythology and thereby the way of feeling and the imagination of the people is completely taken away.

The lovely play of a Hölty, Bürger, Musäus in this field is probably entirely lost for our people, since, in order to be receptive to the enjoyment of it, it is too far behind in its remaining culture, just as the imagination of the more educated parts of the nation has a completely different domain from that of the common estates, and writers and artists who work for the former are absolutely not understood by the latter even as regards the scene and the persons, — whereas the Athenian citizen, whom his poverty excluded from the capacity to give his voice in the public assembly of the people, or who even had to sell himself as a slave, knew as well as a Pericles and an Alcibiades who the Agamemnon and the Oedipus was, whom a Sophocles and Euripides brought onto the stage in noble forms of a beautiful and sublime humanity, or whom a Phidias and Apelles presented in pure shapes of bodily beauty.
zh: 这样一来，既没有会在我们土地上生长起来、与我们的历史相连的宗教想象力，又根本没有一切政治想象力，在普通民众中间就只有这里那里地游荡着一点自己想象力的残余，顶着迷信这个名字——它作为鬼怪信仰，还保存着一座小山的记忆，从前有骑士在那里胡作非为，或者保存着一所房子的记忆，那里有修士和修女闹鬼，或者那里有一个被看作不忠的管家或邻居，在坟墓里还没得到安宁；——或者它作为不从历史中汲取的想象力的产儿，用女巫法力的可能性戏弄软弱或坏的人，——这是尝试过的独立自主和尝试过的财产的贫乏而可悲的残余，而把这些残余彻底铲除，被表象为整个开明的民族阶层的义务，并且是普遍的口吻，——通过民族中较精细部分的这种心情，除了材料本身的不可塑造和粗糙之外，把神话的那点残余、并由此把民族的感受方式和想象力加以提升的可能性，就被完全拿掉了。

赫尔蒂、毕尔格、穆塞乌斯在这个领域里那些可爱的游戏，对我们的民族来说大概完全失掉了，因为民族要享受它们，在其余的教养上还太落后；同样，民族中较有教养的那些部分的想象力，与普通等级的想象力是完全不同的领域，为前者写作的作家和艺术家，后者根本一点也不理解，连在场景和人物上也完全不懂，——与此相反，雅典的市民，哪怕贫穷剥夺了他在公开的民众大会上发言的能力，哪怕他甚至不得不把自己卖为奴隶，他也像伯里克利和阿尔喀比亚德一样清楚，阿伽门农和俄狄浦斯是谁——索福克勒斯和欧里庇得斯以美好而崇高的人性的高贵形式把他们搬上舞台，或者菲迪亚斯和阿佩莱斯以肉体美的纯粹形态把他们表现出来。

en: The truth of the characters in the presentation through Shakespeare has, besides the fact that many of them are known from history, impressed the same so deeply on the English people and formed for it a circle of its own of imaginative representations, that the people, at the exhibitions of the academic paintings, understands well and can freely enjoy the objects of that part where the greatest masters compete, the Shakespeare Gallery.
zh: 莎士比亚的描绘中那些性格的真实，除了其中许多是历史上为人熟知这一点之外，还把它们如此深地印在英国民族身上，并为它形成了一个自己独有的想象表象圈子，以至于民族在学院绘画的展出上，能很好地理解并自由地享受那个部分的对象——最伟大的大师们在那里竞相争胜，也就是莎士比亚画廊。

en: That sphere of imaginative representations which would be common to the educated and to the uneducated part of our nation, religious history, has for poetic treatment, through which the nation could be ennobled, apart from other inconveniences, in regard to the less educated part [the disadvantage] that the latter clings too stiffly to the material as to a matter of faith, in regard to the more educated part [the disadvantage] that, even with a more beautiful treatment on the poet's part, the names already in part carry with them the representation of something old-fashioned and Gothic, in part, on account of the compulsion with which they have from youth on been announced to reason, bring with them a feeling of unease that is contrary to the enjoyment of beauty which proceeds from the free play of the powers of the soul; even if in individual heads the imagination has set itself at liberty and strives after the beautiful and the great alone, one sees it on the whole from their ideals, or from their receptivity to these, that they have been cut to fit it by the catechism.
zh: 那种本来会是我们的民族中受过教养的部分和没受过教养的部分共有的想象表象领域，也就是宗教历史，对于那种能够使民族得到提升的诗意加工来说，除了别的麻烦之外，在较没教养的部分那里[有]这个坏处：它太僵硬地粘在材料上，把材料当作信仰的事情；在较有教养的部分那里[有]这个坏处：即使诗人处理得更美，那些名字本身也已经一方面带有某种老派而哥特式东西的表象，另一方面由于它们从少年时起就被宣布给理性，带来一种不舒服的感受，这种感受与那种从灵魂诸力的自由游戏中产生出来的对美的享受相抵触；即使在个别人的头脑里想象力已经自由地放开了自己、只追求美和伟大的东西，从整体上看，从他们的理想或者他们对这些理想的接受能力上还是看得出，这些理想是按教义问答裁剪得合于想象力的。

en: When the taste for ancient literature, and with it the taste for the fine arts, spread, the more educated part of the nation took the mythology of the Greeks up into its imagination, and its receptivity to these representations proves its greater independence and its independence from the understanding, which otherwise could never refrain from disturbing it in its free enjoyment.
Others attempted to give the Germans back an imagination of their own that had grown on their own ground and soil, and called out to them: is Achaia then the fatherland of the Teutons?

But this imagination is not the imagination of present-day Germans; to restore the lost imagination of a nation was from of old in vain and on the whole could have even less success than Julian's attempt to give the mythology of his forefathers back its former strength and generality in the men of his time, an attempt whose success had much more probability for itself, since much of it still remained in men's minds, since the emperor still had many means at his disposal to give his mythology the preference.

That old-German imagination finds nothing in our age to which it could nestle and attach itself, it stands so torn off in the whole circle of our representations, opinions and beliefs, and is as foreign to us as the Ossianic or the Indian one, and what that poet calls out to his people in regard to Greek mythology, one could with just the same right call out to him and to his people in regard to the Jewish one, and ask: is Judea then the fatherland of the Teutons?
zh: 当对古代文学的趣味、并因此对美的艺术的趣味扩展开来时，民族中较有教养的部分就把希腊人的神话接纳进了自己的想象力，而它对这类表象的接受能力，证明了它有更大的独立自主、更不依赖知性，而知性否则是从来忍不住要在它自由享受时去打扰它的。
另一些人则试着把一种在他们自己的土地上生长起来的、独有的想象力重新还给德意志人，并对他们喊道：亚该亚难道是图伊斯孔人的祖国吗？
可是这种想象力并不是现在德意志人的想象力；把一个民族失去了的想象力重新恢复起来，从来都是徒劳的，而且从整体上看比尤利安的尝试更不可能成功——尤利安曾试图在他那个时代的人身上，把他祖先的神话恢复成从前的力量和普遍性；这个尝试的成功本来有更多可能的理由，因为人们心里还剩下许多这种东西，因为皇帝手里还有许多手段，可以让他的神话得到优先。
那种古老的德意志想象力在我们的时代里找不到任何可以依偎、可以连接的东西，它在我们全部表象、意见和信仰的圈子里显得那么孤零零地断裂着，对我们来说就像莪相的或印第安人的想象力一样陌生；而那位诗人就希腊神话向他的民族喊出的那些话，人们也可以用同样的权利就犹太神话向他和他的民族喊出，并且问：犹地亚难道是图伊斯孔人的祖国吗？

en: However much imagination loves freedom, it is just as much part of it that the religious imagination of a people be firm, that it tie its system less to definite times than to certain known places; this knowledge of the place is for the people usually one proof more, or the surest proof, that the history that one tells about it is true.

Hence the living presence with which the mythology of the Greeks was in their minds; hence the strength of the Catholics' faith in their saints and miracle-workers; to the Catholics those miracles are much more present and more important that were performed in their land than the often much greater ones that were performed in other lands, or those that were performed even by Christ.
Every country usually has its patron saint, who has performed miracles especially in this country and is there venerated above all.

Moreover every people believes itself especially distinguished and honoured by the particular attention that such a patron god has devoted to it, and this pre-eminence over other peoples increases its attachment to it, as is the case with the Jews.
In this way such an imagination becomes native to a people.

That which in our holy books is proper history, as is the greater part of the Old Testament, and does not, like the New Testament, properly have the obligation of faith upon itself, and thus can properly become the object of the people's imagination, is so foreign to our customs, our constitution, the culture of our bodily and spiritual powers, that there is almost no point where we meet with it, except here and there universal human nature — and [is] for everyone who begins to be enlightened, i.e. to demand universality for the laws of his understanding and of his experience — and the number of this class of men is always rising — for the most part unpalatable and fit for use by only two classes of readers, for the one, which with holy simplicity takes everything as true in the sense that it is convinced it would also have been accessible to general experience, and for the other class, to which this question about truth and untruth for the understanding never occurs at all, but which thinks merely of subjective, of truth for the imagination, just as we read them at Herder's hand.58)
zh: 想象力无论多么喜爱自由，一个民族的宗教想象力要稳固，也同样属于它的题中之义：它把自己的体系更少地系于确定的时间，而更多地系于某些为人熟知的地方；对这种地方的熟悉，对民族来说通常多一个证明，或者就是最可靠的证明——证明人们关于它讲述的那段历史是真的。
所以希腊人的神话在他们心中那种活生生的在场；所以天主教徒对他们圣徒和行奇迹者的信仰那么强；对天主教徒来说，那些在他们本国施行的奇迹，比起那些常常大得多、在别的国土上施行的奇迹，或者比起基督亲自施行的奇迹，要切近得多、也重要得多。
每个国家通常都有自己的主保圣人，他尤其在这个国家里行过奇迹，在那里受到格外的崇敬。
此外，每个民族都相信，由于这样一位守护神对它倾注的特别关注，自己格外受抬举、受尊敬，而这种在别的民族面前的优先地位又增强了它对它的依恋，犹太人的情形就是如此。
这样一来，这样一种想象力就在一个民族那里变得土生土长。

我们那些圣书里真正属于历史的东西，比如《旧约》的大部分，而不像《新约》那样本身真正负有信仰义务，因此真正能够成为民族想象力的对象，对我们的风俗、我们的宪法、我们身体力量和灵魂力量的教养来说，却是那么陌生，以至于我们几乎找不到一点能与它相遇的地方，除了这里那里普遍的人性——而且[它]对于每个开始变得开明的人，也就是要求给他的知性和他的经验的法则以普遍性的人——这一类人的数目还在不断增长——，大部分都无法享用，只能供两类读者使用：一类以神圣的单纯在那个意义上把一切都当作真的，确信它对普遍经验本来也是可通达的；另一类则根本不会想到这里关于知性上的真理与不真理的问题，而只想到主观的、想到对想象力而言的真理，就像我们牵着赫尔德的手读它们那样。58)

en: The Greeks had their religious legends almost only in order to have gods to whom they could consecrate their gratitude, to whom they could build altars and bring sacrifices; for us, on the other hand, the sacred history is supposed to be of many uses, we are supposed to learn and gather many things from it in a moral respect.

But a healthy moral power of judgement that sets to work with this intention is very often compelled to put the moral into most stories before it can find anything moral, and with very many it will get into embarrassment altogether about uniting them with its principles.

The main use and the main effect that a pious man can feel in himself in this is edification, i.e. the awakening of dark holy feelings (because he now deals with representations of God), whose confusion renounces any gain in moral insight, but usually brings back with it a strengthening of other so-called holy passions, such as a misunderstood holy zeal for God's honour, pious pride and self-conceit, and a God-resigned sleepiness.
zh: 希腊人几乎只是为了有神可拜才有他们的宗教传说：他们可以把自己的感恩献给这些神，给它们筑祭坛、献祭；相反，神圣历史对我们却应当有多种用处，我们应当在道德方面从中学到、看出许多东西。
可是，一种健全的道德判断力，如果抱着这个打算去动手，就常常不得不先把道德的东西塞进大多数故事里，然后才能找到一点道德的东西；而对相当多的故事，它根本就会为难，没法把它们和自己的原则结合起来。
一个虔诚的人在此之中能在自己身上感到的主要益处和主要效果，就是感化，也就是唤起模糊的圣洁感受（因为他现在是在和关于上帝的表象打交道），这种感受的含混放弃了道德洞见上的收获，却通常又带回来另外一些所谓圣洁激情的增强，比如对上帝荣耀的一种被误解的圣洁热心、虔诚的骄傲和自负，以及一种听命于上帝的嗜睡。
